_comment: Anti-regression guard for the DELETED wrapper entry points `connect()` and
`host()`. Both SDK test suites load this file and scan `roots` (walked
recursively, filtered by `ext`) plus the individual `files` for `patterns`:
python/tests/docs/test_doc_examples.py and typescript/tests/unit/examples.test.ts.
The old guards grepped four exact import strings in docs/**/*.md only, so they
missed .mdx, every call shape, every `webagents.portal` reference, and every
mention inside shipped source - including a public docstring and a runtime
console warning that told developers to call functions that no longer exist.
`files` exists because the most-read docs in the repo are single top-level
markdown files - the three package READMEs go out with the npm and PyPI
packages - and their directories cannot be roots (walking `python/` would
descend into .venv, walking `.` into node_modules). Both test trees are roots
too: a stale reference in a TEST docstring is how the review found one the
guard could not see.
A hit is a failure UNLESS the exact stripped line is listed in `allowlist`.
Allowlist only DELIBERATE narrative about the removed API (a comment saying it
is gone and what replaced it), or a string PLANTED to prove the guard fires.
Never allowlist a line that tells a reader to CALL it. Matching is on the exact
stripped line, so rewording a narrative line re-raises it for review rather
than silently keeping the exemption.
